overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers filed under “Manufacture of Rubber—Japan.” It indexes two items: a 1943 report from Chiba at Chungking concerning new Japanese uses for rubber, and an August 11 item associated with Gentle and Britain concerning Japanese rubber, including a memorandum of a conference attended by Fowler Hamilton and Allison at the Ministry of Economic Affairs with Horton, formerly of the Dunlop Fire Company of Japan, and a sketch locating factories in the Kyoto district.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on rubber manufacture in Japan
subfiles.about: An index sheet identifies two papers concerning Japanese rubber uses, industrial discussions, and factories in the Kyoto district.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a 1943 communication from Chiba at Chungking reporting new Japanese uses for rubber. It also lists an August 11 item associated with Gentle and Britain that included a copy of a conference memorandum involving Fowler Hamilton, Allison, and Horton at the Ministry of Economic Affairs. Horton, formerly of the Dunlop Fire Company of Japan, also supplied a sketch showing the locations of certain factories in the Kyoto district.

interest: This sheet is useful as a compact provenance and contents guide to records that are not themselves reproduced in the surviving page. It points to wartime Allied or diplomatic intelligence about Japan’s adaptation of rubber and identifies Horton, a former employee of a Japanese Dunlop enterprise, as a source of factory-location information. The reference to an accompanying Kyoto factory sketch suggests that the underlying memorandum may have contained unusually specific industrial-geographic intelligence.
